rebuttal_or_critique: I must strongly disagree with the arguments for a rate cut or a shift to a neutral stance. While core inflation at 3.10% is encouraging, it is the headline CPI of 4.75% that dictates the inflation expectations of the common citizen. With food inflation persistently high at 8.69%, any premature easing risks unanchoring these expectations, especially when the economy is operating with a positive output gap of 0.40%. The argument that real rates are 'excessively restrictive' ignores the reality that we are still in the process of bringing inflation durably to the 4.00% target. A shift to neutral or a rate cut at this juncture would be a signal of complacency that we cannot afford. We must remain committed to the withdrawal of accommodation until we see a sustained and significant decline in food price volatility and headline inflation.
